judgments.concern: The scenario names the pallet pose, the pallet width, height, and depth in metres, and which detected pallets are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred. The handling process uses those while the scene can still change. This pocket_opening_depth proposal, the first of the two with this id, publishes width and height as the factory face estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2 already matches, params.pallet_width_m 1.20 m and params.pallet_height_m 0.14 m, and the search template stays that face. The scenario leaves that factory face as the pallet face. Writing width_m and height_m on the stage-2 outcome and on PalletPoseStamped, after input_depth_stamp, places that face on the pose result the handling process reads. The rich message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the sizes belong to this capture. The face-centre position and yaw stay the pose, and pose.position.z stays the range of that centre. Depth is the median far-side length, through the two fork openings the prototype already cuts, of the sample_face_points returns that land inside either pocket rectangle after the pose is removed and whose signed distance lies beyond plane_inlier_threshold_m on the side farther from the camera. The factory face has width and height and no depth parameter. That median is a length along the normal behind the face, which is the depth the scenario lists beside width and height. The user named the three sizes. The part they did not name is the pocket median and has_body_depth. sample_face_points keeps the depth returns inside the detection mask, so a far-side point in a pocket can be the pallet body, a load, the floor, or another object, and that median is what the handling process would take as the pallet depth. When the set is empty, has_body_depth is false, the pose is still published with the factory width and height, and depth_m counts as a body length only when the flag is true. A successful estimate can reach the handling process with the factory face and no body depth. The scenario states no rule that a missing body is a flag, and no rule that the pocket median is the pallet depth. The rejected inlier_face_extents took width and height from the inlier spans and depth from the mean z of those inliers. This proposal publishes the factory face and takes depth from the pocket openings. Which detections are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred stays off the message. Stage 2 still estimates the one candidate select_detection already chooses. A failed estimate publishes no PalletPoseStamped. The two early returns in on_pair stay silent. The other proposal with this same feature id publishes width and height as the greater of the inlier silhouette and the factory face. This one publishes the factory face on every success.

The scenario names the pallet width, height, and depth in metres separately from the pallet pose, for the pallet the vehicle handles while the scene can still change. This second pocket_opening_depth proposal publishes width as the greater of the inlier silhouette and params.pallet_width_m, and height as the greater of the silhouette and params.pallet_height_m. The silhouette is the max-minus-min of this frame's plane inliers on the prototype axes after a shift by minus best_pose.tx and best_pose.ty and a rotation by minus best_pose.theta_rad. A silhouette inside the factory 1.20 m by 0.14 m is published as that factory face, so a cropped plane stays the face the match used. A silhouette past that face is published as the longer span. The search template stays 1.20 m by 0.14 m, and the pose stays the face centre and yaw of that match. The scenario leaves the factory face as the pallet face. The changing-scene sentence means a later frame can already have moved. It states no rule that an inlier span past 1.20 m by 0.14 m is a larger pallet. Those inliers are the plane points inside the detection box, so the extra span can be structure past the pallet, and the handling process would size the approach from a width or height the chamfer match did not use. Depth is the median far-side length of the sample_face_points inside the two pocket rectangles the pose already places. When that set is empty, has_body_depth is false and depth_m is not given as 0, while width and height are still published. The handling process then has a face size, and it still lacks the body depth the scenario lists. The same mask samples can be the pallet body or another surface. The user named the three sizes. The part they did not name is that a short silhouette stays the factory face, and that depth is the pocket median. The rejected inlier_face_extents published the inlier span itself as the pallet size. This proposal publishes a span past the factory face and keeps the factory face when the span is shorter. Which detections are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred stays off the message. Stage 2 still runs once, on the one candidate select_detection already chooses. A failed estimate publishes no PalletPoseStamped. The two early returns stay silent.

The scenario names which detected pallets are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred, and the handling process uses that split while the scene can still change. published_admission_split ranks this capture's class-matched DetectionCandidate list with the strategy select_detection already implements. The ranking uses the first-maximum rule std::max_element already uses, so a tie keeps the earlier candidate and the later tied candidate stays deferred. It admits at most the count the caller passes. The pose node passes one, so stage 2 still estimates that single pallet, and every other candidate in this array stays on deferred, in candidate-list order, each with its source_index. The admitted source index and the deferred source indices are written on PalletPoseStamped after input_depth_stamp. That message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so both sides of the named split sit on the pose result for this capture. The user named the split. The part they did not name is that the split is these two admission vectors, ordered by that first-maximum rule, on that pose result. The scenario asks for a pallet pose, and a count of one is that one pallet. The scenario states no rule that the count changes because the scene can move. When the estimate fails, no PalletPoseStamped is published and the same two lists are written on the failure diagnostic, the only result that path publishes. The scenario states no rule that a failed estimate must still publish the rich pose. The rejected stage2_subset_admission left those vectors with the caller. This proposal writes them on the pose result and on the failure diagnostic. The rejected largest_face_admission sent two faces. This proposal admits the one candidate the node's count asks for. The two early returns that publish nothing stay as they are. The depth-image return already holds a chosen candidate and the other candidates, and that return publishes nothing, so this capture's split never reaches the handling process. An empty candidate list returns both vectors empty and still publishes nothing. An unknown strategy throws, as select_detection already does. Width, height, and depth stay off both results. The pose that is published is still the face centre and yaw of the one admitted pallet. The prior cycle's sent_deferred_roster was not kept, and PalletPoseStamped still carries neither index list.
